rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument begins from what the polytheists must concede: God alone originated creation.
rows.anchor: استدلال بما لا يسعهم إلا الاعتراف به وهو بدء الخلق إذ لا ينازعون في أن الله وحده هو خالق الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is embedded as an a fortiori inference: whoever concedes the first creation should more readily concede its repetition.
rows.anchor: إذا سلم له بدء الخلق كان تسليم إعادته أولى وأجدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After successive past and present nations, their fates illustrate return after death; recalling the deniers’ worldly end prepares a persuasive case for resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: ناسب في مقام الاعتبار أن يقام لهم الاستدلال على إمكان البعث ليقع ذكر ما يعقبه من الجزاء موقع الإقناع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing the divine name before the verbal predicate serves emphasis alone.
rows.anchor: وتقديم اسم الجلالة على المسند الفعلي لمجرد التقوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ثم marks rank rather than time: return to God is greater than re-creation because it is the ultimate purpose of both creation and resurrection.
rows.anchor: هنا للتراخي الرتبي كما هو شأنها في عطف الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the polytheists shifts from third-person reference to direct address.
rows.anchor: فالخطاب في { ترجعون } للمشركين على طريقة الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

rows.speaker: الجمهور وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب
rows.claim: Most readers use second-person تاء ترجعون; Abu Amr, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Rawh from Yaqub read third-person ياء, matching the preceding context.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { ترجعون } بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following account of the criminals’ state when returned to God explains the return and connects especially with the fate of evildoers in the previous verse.
rows.anchor: تبيينا لحال المشركين في وقت ذلك الإرجاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of the expected explicit phrase ‘the day you return,’ the text supplies a clause that clarifies return as occurring when the Resurrection is established, increasing alarm and awe; repetition of the temporal phrase reinforces this.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن تقدير الجملة المضاف إليها { يوم التي يدل عليها إليه ترجعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الساعة commonly denotes the time of gathering and reckoning; its basic sense is a span of time whose extent is fixed by annexation or definiteness.
rows.anchor: وشاع إطلاق { الساعة على وقت الحشر والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah opens the Luqman account by honoring him as a recipient of wisdom and commanding gratitude for that favor.
rows.anchor: وابتدىء ذكر لقمان بالتنويه بأن آتاه الله الحكمة وأمره بشكر النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman’s counsel warns against associating partners, commands kindness to parents and awareness of God, prayer, enjoining right, forbidding wrong and patience, and rejects pride while urging humility in walking and speech.
rows.anchor: من التحذير من الإشراك ، ومن الأمر ببر الوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah weaves reminders of God’s oneness and favors, the polytheists’ rejection of guidance and ancestral imitation, Islam’s merit, and consolation that the faithful hold firmly while the Messenger need not grieve disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وأدمج في ذلك تذكير المشركين بدلائل وحدانية الله تعالى وبنعمه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah answers those who oppose the Quran here and onward, then ends by warning against Satan’s summons and false soothsayer claims to know the unseen.
rows.anchor: وانتظم في هذه السورة الرد على المعارضين للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conditionally, if Quraysh’s question about Luqman and his son occasioned the surah, these verses through 31:12 introduce the story’s knowledge, wisdom, and guidance for believers; the question thus benefited them.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت هذه السورة نزلت بسبب سؤال قريش عن لقمان وابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to the surah’s forthcoming contents, mentally anticipated before their mention.
rows.anchor: والإشارة ب { تلك } إلى ما سيذكر في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آيات الكتاب is the predicate of the demonstrative noun.
rows.anchor: وآيات الكتاب } خبر عن اسم الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distant demonstrative elevates the verses, while their attribution to the wise Book, described as guidance and mercy, signals their worth and their role in success.
rows.anchor: وفي الإشارة تنبيه على تعظيم قدر تلك الآيات بما دل عليه اسم الإشارة من البعد المستعمل في رفعة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation is evidence against those who reject His signs: as creator of all creatures, He alone deserves divinity; assigning it to what creates nothing explains their rejection of the wise Book.
rows.anchor: استئناف للاستدلال على الذين دأبهم الإعراض عن آيات الله بأن الله هو خالق المخلوقات فلا يستحق غيره أن تثبت له الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating idols as comparable to God in attributes implies denying divine wisdom, since wisdom is absent from the idols.
rows.anchor: فهم لما أثبتوا الإلهية لما لا يخلق شيئا كانوا كمن يزعم أن الأصنام مماثلة لله تعالى في أوصافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument is ‘proof of proof’ (tadqīq): it presents a thing with its evidence and the evidence for that evidence.
rows.anchor: ولذا فإن موقع هذه الآيات موقع دليل الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address in ترونها and بكم is directed to the polytheists.
rows.anchor: فالخطاب في قوله { ترونها } و { بكم } للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means ‘for fear that the earth sway beneath you’ or ‘so it does not sway you,’ as explained in the earlier parallel.
rows.anchor: والمعنى خوف أن تميد بكم أو لئلا تميدكم كما بين هنالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised heavens without visible supports recalls the parallel in al-Ra‘d.
rows.anchor: في سورة الرعد قوله : { الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains preventing the earth from swaying recall the parallel in al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: وتقدم في أول سورة النحل قوله وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispersal of creatures has a precedent in al-Baqara’s paired mention of creatures and wind patterns.
rows.anchor: في سورة البقرة قوله : { وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain wording resembles descriptions in al-Baqara and al-Ra‘d.
rows.anchor: في سورة البقرة { وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to God’s first-person plural emphasizes this widely experienced blessing.
rows.anchor: للاهتمام بهذه النعمة التي هي أكثر دورانا عند الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun فيها refers to the earth.
rows.anchor: وضمير { فيها } عائد إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زوج means a kind or species, as in parallel plant descriptions in Ṭā Hā and al-Ḥajj.
rows.anchor: في طه وقوله وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كريم means precious or excellent within its kind, as in the Queen’s description of a precious book.
rows.anchor: تقدم عند قوله تعالى إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم في سورة النمل

words: فَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs also embed favors: animals supply food, milk, wool, hides and transport; plants supply grain, fruit, fodder and truffles; sea creatures benefit people too. Creation thus displays both wisdom and mercy.
rows.anchor: فإن من الدواب المبثوثة ما ينتفع به الناس من أكل لحوم أوانسها ووحوشها والانتفاع بألبانها وأصوافها وجلودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that this is God’s creation concludes the evidence from the heavens, earth, mountains, creatures, rain and plants.
rows.anchor: وجملة { هذا خلق الله } إلى آخرها نتيجة الاستدلال بخلق السماء والأرض والجبال والدواب وإنزال المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular demonstrative treats the listed creation collectively as the single thing mentioned.
rows.anchor: والإتيان به مفردا بتأويل المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from first-person narration to third-person naming makes God’s identity as creator explicit.
rows.anchor: والانتقال من التكلم إلى الغيبة في قوله { خلق الله } التفاتا لزيادة التصريح بأن الخطاب وارد من جانب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording again shifts to third person to maintain the return to the third-person frame in خلق الله.
rows.anchor: وكذلك يكون الانتقال من التكلم إلى الغيبة في قوله { ماذا خلق الذين من دونه } التفاتا لمراعاة العود إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If رؤية means knowing or informing, فأروني is suspended from taking an object by the interrogative ماذا; the command is taunting and challenges them to identify any creature made by another.
rows.anchor: أي فأنبئوني ، والفعل معلقا عن العمل بالاستفهام ب { ماذا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using a visual command intensifies the challenge: they would have to produce an object they claim their gods created, though the command also incapacitates them.
rows.anchor: وصوغ أمر التعجيز من مادة الرؤية البصرية أشد في التعجيز لاقتضائها الاقتناع منهم بأن يحضروا شيئا يدعون أن آلهتهم خلقته

rows.speaker: حطائط بن يعفر النهشلي وقيل حاتم الطائي
rows.claim: A line attributed either to Ḥuṭā’iṭ ibn Ya‘far al-Nahshalī or Ḥātim al-Ṭā’ī uses أريني to mean show me a horse that died of starvation, witnessing for visual seeing.
rows.anchor: أريني جوادا مات هزلا لعلني أرى ما تزين أو بخيلا مخلدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab usage commonly intends sensory seeing in this challenge, as in expressions about what one’s eye saw and asking whether someone sees.
rows.anchor: والعرب يقصدون في مثل هذا الغرض الرؤية البصرية

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru’ al-Qays’s line about a separation seen as more distant uses رأى for visual perception.
rows.anchor: فلله عينا من رأى من تفرق أشت وأنأى من فراق المحصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational relative pronoun is applied to idols by accommodating the polytheists’ belief that they are intelligent beings.
rows.anchor: وإجراء اسم موصول العقلاء على الأصنام مجاراة للمشركين إذ يعدونهم عقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دون is a metonym for ‘other’; من is an added preposition before a locative noun, reinforcing its connection to the circumstantial complement.
rows.anchor: و { من دونه } صلة الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل shifts from disputation to recording their error in believing idols divine, as in debate when one sets aside a point and moves to another.
rows.anchor: و { بل } للإضراب الانتقالي من غرض المجادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers here are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: الظالمون : المشركون . والضلال المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their manifest misguidance is grave disbelief: they rejected Islam’s call to truth and associated another with God in divinity.
rows.anchor: الكفر الفظيع ، لأنهم أعرضوا عن دعوة الإسلام للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition conveys that misguidance surrounds and clings to them in all their states.
rows.anchor: وجيء بحرف الظرفية لإفادة اكتناف الضلال بهم في سائر أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw connects Luqman’s guidance and wisdom with al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith’s heedless misguidance in 31:6, forming a contrast between the two men.
rows.anchor: الواو عاطفة قصة لقمان على قصة النضر بن الحارث المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although al-Naḍr’s story began as an introduction, its length makes it an independent subject; the waw links stories rather than presenting a conclusion after premises.
rows.anchor: لما طال في المقدمة خرجت عن سنن المقدمات إلى المقصودات بالذات فلذلك عطفت عطف القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single style can serve multiple rhetorical considerations; the author illustrates this with alternate formulations about Pharaoh’s abuse of the Israelites.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى { يسومونكم سوء العذاب يذبحون أبناءكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story opens with the emphatic oath-lām and قد to announce an important event that has certainly occurred.
rows.anchor: وافتتاح القصة بحرفي التوكيد : لام القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks a ranked transition to the important return to God, after which all will be told what they did; the plural includes both the person and the parents.
rows.anchor: { ثم } للتراخي الرتبي المفيد للاهتمام بما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preposing ‘to Me’ highlights the return or restricts it to God, so the idols they hope in cannot benefit them.
rows.anchor: للاهتمام بهذا الرجوع أو هو للتخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement is a promise and threat; informing is a metonym for displaying recompense, since revealing something makes it known.
rows.anchor: والإنباء كناية عن إظهار الجزاء على الأعمال لأن الملازمة بين إظهار الشيء وبين العلم به ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns combine direct address with reference in the third person, giving priority to address because it is more salient.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الضمائر تغليب الخطاب على الغيبة لأن الخطاب أهم لأنه أعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the vocative renews the listener’s attention for the coming words.
rows.anchor: تكرير النداء لتجديد نشاط السامع لوعي الكلام

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Nāfi‘ and Abū Ja‘far read مثقال in the nominative as the subject of complete kāna.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو جعفر { إن تك مثقال } برفع { مثقال } على أنه فاعل { تك من ( كان ) التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that reading, مثقال takes feminine agreement from its annexed حبة; إنها refers to the event as a feminine pronoun of the matter, a common construction when a feminine term follows.
rows.anchor: وإنما جيء بفعله بتاء المضارعة للمؤنثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun of the matter often follows إن and also serves as the implied subject of lightened أن; it focuses attention on what follows.
rows.anchor: ويكثر وقوع ضمير الشأن بعد ( إن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call, إن and the pronoun of the matter make three emphatic markers, stressing the danger of the claim and establishing God’s comprehensive knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: فاجتمع في هذه الجملة ثلاثة مؤكدات : النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the tiniest, most hidden object in an inaccessible place proves that whatever is more visible and near is all the more within God’s knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: فذكر أدق الكائنات حالا من حيث تعلق العلم والقدرة به

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers put مثقال in the accusative as the predicate of defective kāna, supplying its subject from context; إنها then means the deed, good or bad.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الباقون بنصب { مثقال } على الخبرية ل { تك } من ( كان ) الناقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثقال is an object by which weight is measured, shaped on the pattern of an instrument noun.
rows.anchor: ما يقدر به الثقل ولذلك صيغ على زنة اسم الآلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A حبة is one seed or grain from a plant, including grain or legume, capable of seeding its kind.
rows.anchor: واحدة الحب وهو بذر النبات من سنابل أو قطنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustard is described as a branching plant with small yellow flowers and tiny, sharply pungent seeds; its seeds were widely used in medicinal poultices for internal inflammation, though physicians increasingly replace it.
rows.anchor: ولب تلك البزور شديد الحرارة يلدغ اللسان والجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel in al-Anbiyā’ says that even a mustard seed’s weight is brought forth, reinforcing the same point.
rows.anchor: وتقدم نظير هذا في سورة الأنبياء فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها

words: أَوْ فِى صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are coordinated with the rock as a more inaccessible location, and earth is added to include all terrestrial places; any location is equally within God’s knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: لأن الصخرة من أجزاء الأرض فذكر بعدها { أو في السماوات }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the condemnation of ancestral imitation in 31:21: they inherit polytheism yet acknowledge that God created heaven and earth, exposing their irrational inconsistency.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven and earth encompass their contents, including the stones from which idols are made.
rows.anchor: ما يشمل ما فيها من المخلوقات ومن بين ذلك حجارة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah’s لا يعلمون varies stylistically from al-‘Ankabūt’s لا يعقلون while conveying the same meaning.
rows.anchor: تفننا في المخالفة بين القصتين مع اتحاد المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership is the conclusion implied by the prior admission that He created heaven and earth; the sentence is a result and an inclusive apposition to what precedes, as in the reasoning at 31:16.
rows.anchor: موقع هذه الجملة من التي قبلها موقع النتيجة من الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit conclusion belittles their disbelief: God owns them and everything around them, including their idols, and is self-sufficient and praised apart from their worship.
rows.anchor: والتصريح بهذه النتيجة لقصد التهاون بهم في كفرهم بأن الله يملكهم ويملك ما في السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هو is a separating pronoun that restricts self-sufficiency and praise to God, excluding the supposed gods.
rows.anchor: اختصاص الغنى والحمد بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier assertions of God’s knowledge of hidden things in the counsel and in 31:23 lead into this account of the reach of divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: تكرر فيما سبق من هذه السورة وصف الله تعالى بإحاطة العلم بجميع الأشياء ظاهرة وخفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reveals some knowledge to chosen messengers when wisdom requires it and keeps other knowledge to Himself when wisdom requires withholding it.
rows.anchor: بإثبات أن لعلم الله تعالى مظاهر يبلغ بعضها إلى من اصطفاه من رسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God chose to communicate all that He knows, even creatures fit to record His words could not contain it, much less could oral transmission suffice.
rows.anchor: وأنه لو شاء أن يبلغ ما في علمه لما وفت به مخلوقاته الصالحة لتسجيل كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories of Luqman here and the People of the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn in al-Kahf prepare for that surah’s parallel image of the sea as ink, closely resembling this verse.
rows.anchor: فعقبتا بقوله في آخر السورة : { قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي

rows.speaker: أصحاب التأويل من السلف من أصحاب ابن عباس
rows.claim: Early interpreters associated with Ibn ‘Abbās explain the otherwise obscure placement of this verse in its context.
rows.anchor: أخذ أصحاب التأويل من السلف من أصحاب ابن عباس في بيان إيقاع هذه الآية في هذا الموقع

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن يسار
rows.claim: Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr, ‘Ikrima, and ‘Aṭā’ ibn Yasār report with near variants that Jews questioned the Prophet, or prompted Quraysh to question him, after 17:85; they objected that the Torah explains everything. He replied that it is little beside God’s knowledge, then these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وعطاء بن يسار بروايات متقاربة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī reports that Quraysh complained that Muhammad spoke too much, and these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: ما أكثر كلام محمد فنزلت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports Quraysh said Muhammad’s speech would end or run out, and the verse was revealed; another narration phrases it as ‘this speech will run out.’
rows.anchor: سيتم هذا الكلام لمحمد وينحسر أي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فلا يقول بعده كلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports imply a Medinan revelation, requiring prophetic direction to place the verse here for its thematic fit; others imply a Meccan revelation inserted after earlier verses as Luqman was revealed.
rows.anchor: وهذه يرجع بعضها إلى أن هذه الآية نزلت بالمدينة فيلزم أن يكون وضعها في هذا الموضع من السورة بتوقيف نبوي للمناسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلمات is a plural meaning speech: God’s utterances to angels and other creatures, His creative command Be, and revelation to prophets from the earliest times through Muhammad.
rows.anchor: و { كلمات } جمع كلمة بمعنى الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if every tree became writing pens and the sea and added seas supplied ink, all the pens and ink would be exhausted while God’s words remained inexhaustible.
rows.anchor: أن يكتب كلامه كله صحفا ففرضت الأشجار كلها مقسمة أقلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The completion of God’s words in 6:115 means their fulfillment and effectiveness; al-Anfāl likewise speaks of God establishing truth by His words.
rows.anchor: فالتمام هنالك بمعنى التحقق والنفوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise, artful argument begins with لو to mark its content as a hypothetical; the author refers to Sībawayh’s usage as discussed in Mughnī al-Labīb and to another Quranic example.
rows.anchor: وقد نظمت هذه الآية بإيجاز بديع إذ ابتدئت بحرف لو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من شجرة explains the relative ما as a specification and therefore remains singular rather than أشجار.
rows.anchor: بيان ل { ما } الموصولة وهو في معنى التمييز فحقه الإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A قلم is a split reed for holding ink and writing; each tree is imagined as supplying as many pens as it has suitable branches, and the plural can denote few or many.
rows.anchor: ليرفع به المداد ويكتب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an open ياء and ḍamma on ميم, يمده means to increase the sea’s ink; it presumes the sea is ink and more seas replenish it as it dries, a concise sense lost with أمده.
rows.anchor: بفتح الياء التحتية وضم الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven often stands idiomatically for a great number, as in the Prophet’s saying that an unbeliever eats in seven intestines; the number is not restrictive.
rows.anchor: تستعمل في الكناية عن الكثرة كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما نفدت means God’s words do not end; this refutes Jews who treat the Torah as the limit of His words.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ما نفدت كلمات الله } ما انتهت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same image can answer polytheists who think the Quran’s revelation is nearly finished; on this reading, God’s words mean the Quran and exaggerate how much more will be revealed.
rows.anchor: أو كيف يحسب المشركون أن ما نزل من القرآن أوشك أن يكون انتهاء القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause is a summation: God’s might defeats those awaiting the Prophet’s embarrassment, and His wisdom has no end, so neither do His words.
rows.anchor: فهو لعزته لا يغلبه الذين يزعمون عدم الحاجة إلى القرآن

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers put البحر in the nominative as a circumstantial nominal clause describing the trees while the sea is their ink; the circumstantial waw links the simultaneous state without a pronoun.
rows.anchor: على أن الجملة الاسمية في موضع الحال والواو واو الحال

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abū ‘Amr and Ya‘qūb read البحر in the accusative, coordinating it with the noun of إن.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب { والبحر } بالنصب عطفا على اسم ( إن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of equal ease in creating and resurrecting connects to 31:23’s return and accounting; scripture often answers doubts about bodily resurrection after mentioning it.
rows.anchor: لأنه كلما ذكر أمر البعث هجس في نفوس المشركين استحالة إعادة الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents argued that people are formed in stages, so reviving all nations and generations at once seemed impossible; Abū ibn Khalaf, Abū al-Asad (or Abū al-Asadayn), and Nabīh and Munabbih ibn al-Ḥajjāj of Banū Sahm said this, perhaps privately.
rows.anchor: يقولون ذلك وربما أسر به بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural addresses all humanity generically: creating and raising all people is like creating or raising one person, since complete power treats few and many, origination and return alike.
rows.anchor: وضميرا المخاطبين مراد بهما جميع الخلق فهما بمنزلة الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to direct address confronts the opponents with a decisive argument.
rows.anchor: التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب لقصد مجابهتهم بالاستدلال المفحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted noun is understood: the creation and resurrection of one soul, an ellipsis signaled by ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم; al-Nābigha’s verse similarly omits the noun ‘fear’ before its comparison.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { كنفس واحدة } حذف مضاف دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible function is to explain God’s power: His encompassing knowledge of objects, causes and particulars enables action as He wills; opponents’ admission that He knows everything persuades them of His power.
rows.anchor: التعليل لكمال القدرة على ذلك الخلق العجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase answers the inward astonishment of people who privately denied resurrection, as anticipated by 31:23; that is why the verse says ‘hearing, seeing’ rather than ‘knowing, powerful.’
rows.anchor: موقع الاستئناف البياني لما ينشأ عن الإخبار
